quote: Several concepts have been proposed to define plant biostimulants. Basak (2008), proposed that biostimulants could be classified depending on the mode of action and the origin of the active ingredient while Bulgari et al. (2015), proposed that “biostimulants should be classified on the basis of their action in the plants or, on the physiological plant responses rather than on their composition.” Du Jardin (2015), however, has emphasized the importance of the final impact on plant productivity when he suggests that “any definition of biostimulants should focus on the agricultural functions of biostimulants, not on the nature of their constituents nor on their modes of actions.”

value: A DEFINITION BUILT ON IRREDUCIBILITY: the effect must come from emergent properties of the whole complex and NOT be the sole consequence of any known constituent - so a product whose activity is explained by its nutrients is, by this definition, not a biostimulant

quote: Substances and materials, with the exception of nutrients and pesticides, which, when applied to plants, seeds or growing substrates in specific formulations, have the capacity to modify physiological processes of plants in a way that provides potential benefits to growth, development and/or stress response.

value: the small-quantity criterion: an organic material whose response cannot be attributed to traditional plant nutrients

value: the safety criterion written into one national definition - no risk to human, animal or natural environment
quote: They mean inorganic and organic substances or its mixtures positively affecting plant development or other physiological processes in plants.

value: a patent-style definition listing bio-stimulatory activity as everything from sugar generation to allelopathy
quote: The term “bio-stimulatory” means according to the invention, if not otherwise specified, an activity or efficacy which stimulates, increases or improves many different processes in the plant or plant parts, such as improved generation of growth promoting substances like sugars and amino acids, improved adequate supply of cells with available nutrients and growth regulators, enhanced cell metabolism, improved cell decontamination, enhanced immune defense, promotion of growth and yield, induction of systemic acquired resistance (SAR), inhibition of growth and yield of competing plants (allelopathy).

value: the phytostimulator definition, which locates the activity in a microorganism that changes growth-regulator concentrations

quote: Agents which at very low concentrations improve the basic biochemical processes in plants and soil, and thereby improve the growth and development of plants, and increase their resistance to stress.
